headline: Compute got more expensive this month while the models that run on it got cheaper. Nebius raised GPU list prices by about a fifth and GMI Cloud funded two thirds of a $668M raise with debt, yet Anthropic cut its flagship token price 20 percent and the best open model now sits 12 index points behind the leader. The margin is moving to whoever owns capacity at one end and the customer's workflow at the other, and 2 December is the next hard date for anyone shipping generated text into Europe.

investors.call: Underwrite neocloud equity on utilisation and the cost of debt, not on the number of GPUs.
investors.why: GMI Cloud funded $445M of its $668M raise with a credit facility, and Nebius lifted H100 list prices from $3.85 to $4.50 on 1 October. Higher list prices help service that debt only for as long as demand outruns supply.
investors.watch: Whether the Nebius increase holds through the next price checks, or new Blackwell capacity pulls list prices back toward September levels.

investors.call: Pay for revenue, not for proximity to the frontier labs.
investors.why: Instinct raised $1B at a $10B valuation without publishing revenue, while EliseAI raised at $4B on more than $200M in annual recurring revenue. At the top, the reported $1.4T OpenAI mark is still only talks, so the sector's reference price is not yet set.
investors.watch: Whether the OpenAI round closes near $1.4T. A lower close or a failed one would reprice every lab and late-stage round marked against it.

investors.call: In AI tooling the likely exit is a strategic buyer, so price tooling deals as future acquisitions.
investors.why: SpaceX closed its $60B purchase of Cursor in August and Nvidia agreed to buy Hugging Face for about $13B in September. Supabase folded in Turso in the same week it raised $150M, so independent tools are being absorbed by the platforms above them.
investors.watch: Whether the Nvidia and Hugging Face deal closes on its announced terms, which would confirm chip vendors as buyers of developer distribution.

bigtech.call: Lock in GPU capacity on contract now, because on-demand rates are rising and the gap between providers is wide.
bigtech.why: Published H100 on-demand rates run from {lo_price} at {lo_provider} to {hi_price} at {hi_provider} ({hi_type} source), a spread of {ratio} times for the same chip. Nebius raised list prices 17 to 21 percent on 1 October and lists commit discounts of up to 35 percent.
bigtech.watch: B200 undercutting H100 per unit of work as Blackwell supply grows, which would favour shorter commitments.

bigtech.call: Assume the model vendors and chip makers now compete for your users and your developers.
bigtech.why: GPT-6 brought a generative interface with charts, forms and buttons to more than 1.2 billion weekly ChatGPT users. Nvidia is buying Hugging Face and SpaceX bought Cursor, so the places developers gather are moving under chip and platform owners.
bigtech.watch: How Nvidia runs Hugging Face after the deal closes, and whether terms change for models built for rival hardware.

bigtech.call: Fund compliance and deployment people ahead of more model spend, since those now gate agent launches.
bigtech.why: Marking for text generators already on the EU market is due on 2 December 2026, and OpenAI is shipping watermarking ahead of it. Anthropic is paying $100M to train 10,000 deployment engineers with the large consultancies, which says the people who put agents into production are the scarce input.
bigtech.watch: Whether US courts let federal action override state AI laws before Colorado's rewritten act applies on 1 January 2027.

builders.call: Rerun your inference cost model this month, because the price floor dropped at every tier.
builders.why: Claude Haiku 5.5 starts at $0.10 per million input tokens, Sonnet 5.5 is at $2 and Opus 5.5 is 20 percent cheaper than Opus 5. The $0.75 Gemini 3.8 Flash rate is introductory and runs only through 31 December 2026, so separate promotional prices from list prices.
builders.watch: Whether Google extends the Gemini 3.8 Flash introductory price past 31 December or lets it step up.

builders.call: Keep an open-weight model as a tested fallback, but price the GPU hours honestly.
builders.why: MiMo-V2.6 Pro is MIT licensed and scores 46 on the Artificial Analysis index against 58 for Opus 5.5. Renting H100s to serve it costs {lo_price} to {hi_price} per GPU-hour on published rates, and Nebius just raised its prices.
builders.watch: DeepSeek confirming the license on V4.1 Flash, and whether its claimed cut in KV cache memory holds up outside the vendor's own tests.

builders.call: Wedge in where agents do the buying or where the work is sold as an outcome, not in the chat front end.
builders.why: Supabase says about 70 percent of its new databases are created by agents, and EliseAI passed $200M in annual recurring revenue selling finished leasing and intake work. GPT-6 put a generative interface in front of more than 1.2 billion weekly users, which leaves a thin chat layer little room.
builders.watch: Which pricing model wins for agents, the seat, the task or the outcome, as more application companies disclose revenue.

thesis.title: The Bottleneck Thesis
thesis.text: In AI, value accrues to whoever controls the scarcest input, and the scarce input keeps moving. Right now there are three. Compute (chips and capacity), capital (who can fund the build, and the rules that decide where money is allowed to go), and energy (the power that runs it all). Every item on this page is tagged by which constraint it moves and in which direction.

key.text: The input got scarcer or harder to access.
The input got easier or cheaper to get.
The input moved hands or is contested.

how_to_read: Each item carries a constraint tag and a direction. Read the board first, then use the filters to see which items move which constraint. Prices, deals, rules and power below are the evidence, and every row links to the page it came from.

board.name: Compute
board.line: Neocloud list prices rose this month and the published H100 spread is {ratio} times.

evidence.text: Nebius lifted H100 to $4.50 and B200 to $8.50 per GPU-hour on 1 Oct, up 17 to 21 percent
One-year H100 contract index rose nearly 40 percent, from $1.70 in Oct 2025 to $2.35 in Mar 2026
On-demand H100 runs from {lo_price} at {lo_provider} to {hi_price} at {hi_provider} ({hi_type} source)

board.flip: Listed prices falling back to September levels for two quarters, or B200 undercutting H100 per unit of work as Blackwell supply grows.

board.name: Capital
board.line: Mega-rounds are getting done, and debt is carrying the infrastructure build.

evidence.text: OpenAI is reportedly seeking at least $30B at about $1.4T before new money (talks only)
Anthropic closed a $65B Series H at $965B post-money on 28 May 2026
GMI Cloud raised $668M, of which $445M was debt
EU Digital Omnibus in force 27 Jul 2026. High-risk duties move to Dec 2027 and Article 50 marking lands 2 Dec 2026 for older systems

board.flip: A mega-round that fails to close or reprices down, or GPU-backed debt that gets harder to place.

board.name: Energy
board.line: Power is booked years ahead. Turbines are sold into the 2030s and the largest US grid market cleared at its price cap again.

evidence.text: Google signed for about 3.6 GW from 11 Constellation nuclear plants on 6 Oct 2026, with 890 MW on a 20-year term from 2028
GE Vernova's gas turbine backlog and reservations reached 116 GW, with data center orders above $5B so far this year
PJM's 2028 to 2029 capacity auction cleared at the $325 per MW-day cap, driven mainly by data center demand

board.flip: Capacity auctions clearing below the cap, or turbine slots opening up inside two years.

audience.investors: Falling token prices compress gross margin for any startup that resells model access, so check how much of a company's value is a markup on tokens.
audience.bigtech: A 20 percent cut at the flagship tier lowers the cost of buying over building and weakens the case for training an in-house model of the same class.
audience.builders: Haiku 5.5 at $0.10 per million input tokens for prompts under 100k tokens makes routing, classification and extraction cheap enough to run on every request.

signals.title: Anthropic cuts its flagship price and ships a ten cent small model
signals.summary: Claude Opus 5.5 launched on 22 September at $4 input and $20 output per million tokens, down from $5 and $25 for Opus 5. Claude Haiku 5.5 followed on 7 October at $0.10 and $0.50 for prompts under 100k tokens.
signals.moves: The buyer's cost of capability. Per-token prices fell 20 percent at the flagship tier and the new small model starts at $0.10 per million input tokens.
signals.why_it_matters: Per-token prices keep falling at every tier, which squeezes any product whose only edge is access to a model.

audience.investors: A generative interface in front of more than 1.2 billion weekly users puts pressure on any startup whose main product is a chat front end.
audience.bigtech: OpenAI now owns a consumer surface that renders forms and buttons, so any assistant you ship competes with it for the same users.
audience.builders: A thin chat interface on top of a model is now weaker than the one the model vendor ships to every ChatGPT tier, so put your effort elsewhere.

signals.title: GPT-6 reaches every ChatGPT tier with a generative interface
signals.summary: OpenAI began rolling out GPT-6 in ChatGPT on 7 October, with Sol behind paid tiers and Luna behind Free and Go. Answers can now include charts, forms and tappable buttons, and OpenAI says ChatGPT has more than 1.2 billion weekly users.
signals.moves: Compute demand. A 1.2 billion weekly user base on a new model keeps inference load, and so GPU demand, rising.
signals.why_it_matters: The interface layer is turning generative, so any team building a chat front end now competes with the model vendor's own UI.

audience.investors: Portfolio companies selling into Europe face a dated compliance cost on 2 December, which is worth raising at the next board meeting.
audience.bigtech: Text marking is becoming a condition of shipping generative features in the EU, so product and legal teams need one provenance plan before December.
audience.builders: If you generate text for EU users, decide now whether to rely on your model vendor's watermark or add your own.

signals.title: OpenAI ships text watermarking ahead of an EU marking deadline
signals.summary: From 5 October API customers can opt in to machine-readable text watermarking, and an EU-only invisible watermark is coming to ChatGPT and Codex. The EU AI Act marking duty applies from 2 December 2026 to systems placed on the market before 2 August.
signals.moves: Deployment rights in the EU. Text marking is becoming a condition of shipping there.
signals.why_it_matters: Provenance is turning into a shipping requirement, and teams selling into Europe need a plan before December.

audience.investors: Infrastructure tools are being folded into larger platforms, so the likely exit in the database layer is a sale to a platform.
audience.bigtech: When agents create most new databases on a platform, the developer you sell to is increasingly an agent, which changes how APIs and pricing should work.
audience.builders: Make your product easy for an agent to provision and use through an API, because agents already create most new databases on Supabase.

signals.title: Supabase buys Turso and says agents create most new databases
signals.summary: Supabase raised $150 million led by GIC and acquired Turso, with terms undisclosed. It says about 70 percent of new databases on its platform are created by agents or AI-driven tools.
signals.moves: Capital toward agent-native infrastructure. The acquisition folds a database primitive into a larger platform.
signals.why_it_matters: Agents are becoming the primary buyer of infrastructure primitives, which changes who the product has to be designed for.

audience.investors: Deployment capacity sits between model spend and revenue, which favours companies that pair software with hands-on rollout in the near term.
audience.bigtech: Anthropic is training deployment engineers with Accenture, Bain, Deloitte and McKinsey, so the talent to roll out agents will increasingly come through vendor programs.
audience.builders: Customers will expect hands-on deployment help, so budget for forward deployed engineers instead of planning a pure self-serve motion.

signals.title: Anthropic commits $100 million to train 10,000 deployment engineers
signals.summary: The Claude Frontier Academy will train Frontier Deployed Engineers through a residency run inside customer organisations. First-cohort partners include Accenture, Bain, Deloitte, McKinsey and Morgan Stanley.
signals.moves: Where capital goes after compute. $100M is aimed at deployment capacity, the scarce skill between a model and a production agent.
signals.why_it_matters: The scarce input is people who can put agents into production, and the vendors are now paying to create them.

audience.investors: With $445 million of the $668 million in debt, returns on neocloud equity now depend on utilisation staying high enough to service credit.
audience.bigtech: Debt-funded capacity in the US, Taiwan and Asia-Pacific adds suppliers to contract with, but their balance sheets belong in the vendor review.
audience.builders: More GPU supply in Taiwan and Asia-Pacific may give you regional options for serving users there.

signals.title: GMI Cloud raises $668 million, most of it debt
signals.summary: The GPU cloud closed a $223 million Series B led by ARCHIV with NVIDIA taking part, plus a $445 million credit facility led by CTBC. It will add capacity in the US, Taiwan and the wider Asia-Pacific region.
signals.moves: How the build is financed. Debt supplied $445M of the $668M, so capacity growth leans on credit.
signals.why_it_matters: Debt is now funding more of the GPU build than equity, which ties neocloud returns to utilisation and interest rates.

audience.investors: A neocloud lifting list prices 17 to 21 percent supports near-term revenue for capacity owners and says demand still outruns supply.
audience.bigtech: Rising on-demand rates strengthen the case for committed capacity, and Nebius lists commit discounts of up to 35 percent.
audience.builders: If you rent H100s on demand, your hosting bill can rise with no change on your side, so keep a second provider tested and ready.

signals.title: Nebius raises GPU list prices by about a fifth
signals.summary: The Nebius price page now shows H100 at $4.50 per GPU-hour, up from $3.85, with H200 at $5.40, B200 at $8.50 and B300 at $9.50. Those are rises of 17 to 21 percent, effective 1 October.
signals.moves: Rental price of H100 to B300 capacity, up 17 to 21 percent in one step.
signals.why_it_matters: A neocloud lifting list prices says demand for accelerated capacity still outruns supply.

audience.investors: A close near $1.4 trillion would reset the reference price for every lab, and a cut or failed close would mark down everyone priced against it.
audience.bigtech: A round of at least $30 billion would fund more compute and more product reach, so expect OpenAI to keep moving into adjacent surfaces.
audience.builders: Well-funded labs will keep cutting prices and shipping features, so any product that depends only on model access stays exposed.

signals.title: OpenAI reportedly seeks $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation
signals.summary: Bloomberg reported on 29 September that OpenAI is in early talks to raise at least $30 billion at about $1.4 trillion before the new money. The talks are not closed and terms could change.
signals.moves: The top of the capital stack. A mark near $1.4 trillion resets the reference price for every lab, if the round closes.
signals.why_it_matters: It sets the entry price for the frontier-lab asset class and the bar every other lab is measured against.

audience.investors: An MIT-licensed model within 12 index points of the leader limits how much closed-model vendors can charge over time.
audience.bigtech: A credible open model makes running open weights in-house a realistic alternative to buying API access for cost-sensitive workloads.
audience.builders: MiMo-V2.6 Pro is a self-hosted fallback with a 1 million token context, worth testing on your most cost-sensitive workloads.

signals.title: Xiaomi releases a trillion-parameter open-weight model under MIT
signals.summary: MiMo-V2.6 Pro has 1.02 trillion total and 42 billion active parameters, a 1 million token context, and weights on Hugging Face. Artificial Analysis scores it 46 on its Intelligence Index, the highest for an open-weight model, against 58 for Claude Opus 5.5.
signals.moves: Dependence on closed-model capacity. An open model within 12 index points can run on rented GPUs.
signals.why_it_matters: A twelve point gap to the closed frontier makes self-hosting a credible option for cost-sensitive workloads.

audience.investors: About $13 billion for the main open model hub shows strategic buyers will pay for developer distribution, which supports exit values for platforms.
audience.bigtech: The leading chip vendor owning the main open model hub is a platform risk for any team whose models or tools depend on Hugging Face.
audience.builders: If your stack depends on Hugging Face hosting or libraries, watch for changed terms once the Nvidia deal closes.

signals.title: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face for about $13 billion
signals.summary: The deal includes an equity retention program of up to $1 billion for employees who join Nvidia. Nvidia frames it as a way to protect open-source AI developers who rely on the platform.
signals.moves: Control of distribution. The chip vendor would own the main hub for open models.
signals.why_it_matters: The dominant chip vendor would own the main distribution hub for open models, a new kind of vertical integration.

takes.headline: Compute is the binding constraint, and the owners of power and capacity keep the margin.
takes.body: Published H100 on-demand prices run from {lo_price} to {hi_price} per GPU-hour, a spread of {ratio} times for the same chip. Nebius lifted its list prices 17 to 21 percent on 1 October, and a one-year H100 contract index rose nearly 40 percent between October 2025 and March 2026. GMI Cloud financed most of its latest raise with debt, so capacity growth now depends on credit as much as on chips. The margin sits with whoever controls electricity, buildings and financing, because the chip is only one of three inputs.
takes.change_my_mind: Listed prices falling back to September levels for two quarters, or B200 undercutting H100 per unit of work as Blackwell supply grows.

takes.headline: Capital is loosening for a few names, and value in agentic software accrues to whoever owns the workflow and the outcome.
takes.body: Anthropic closed $65 billion at $965 billion and OpenAI is reportedly seeking $30 billion more, so money is abundant at the top. Meanwhile the price of model access keeps falling, with Opus 5.5 at 20 percent below Opus 5 and an MIT-licensed open model within 12 index points of the leader. EliseAI reports more than $200 million in annual recurring revenue by selling leasing and patient intake as finished work, and Supabase says agents create about 70 percent of its new databases. Model access is heading toward a commodity, while trust in a specific job is not. Rules now steer that money too. The EU marking duty for text generators lands on 2 December 2026 and Colorado rewrote its AI Act, so capital is flowing to teams that can ship inside those limits.
takes.change_my_mind: Model vendors bundling the workflow themselves. The SpaceX purchase of Cursor is the case to watch.

takes.headline: Power is the new waiting list, and whoever has it booked sets the pace of the build-out.
takes.body: Google signed for about 3.6 GW from 11 Constellation nuclear plants on 6 October, with 890 MW on a 20-year term from 2028. GE Vernova's gas turbine queue reached 116 GW and its order book runs years ahead, while PJM cleared its 2028 to 2029 capacity auction at the $325 cap. Chips can be bought in a quarter. Power takes years.
takes.change_my_mind: Capacity auctions clearing below the cap, or turbine slots opening up inside two years.

layers.name: Silicon
layers.subtitle: Accelerators, memory and the fabs behind them.
layers.bottleneck_now: Packaging, high-bandwidth memory and export licensing decide who gets chips. Published H100 rates still differ by 3 times across providers.
layers.business_model: Sell accelerators and full systems at high margin, while hyperscalers build custom chips to cut their own bill.
layers.structural_bottleneck: Advanced packaging, high-bandwidth memory and the export rules that decide which chips can cross which borders.
layers.question_to_watch: Do custom chips take a meaningful share of inference from GPUs within two years?

sources.label: BIS case-by-case H200 rule, via Introl

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.subtitle: Clouds and data centres that rent the compute.
layers.bottleneck_now: Capacity and the debt that funds it. Nebius raised list prices 17 to 21 percent and GMI Cloud leaned on $445M of credit.
layers.business_model: Hourly GPU rental, committed capacity contracts, and managed inference on top.
layers.structural_bottleneck: Power, grid connection and construction time, more than the chips themselves.
layers.question_to_watch: Will the Nebius price rise hold, or does new Blackwell capacity pull list prices back down?

layers.name: Data
layers.subtitle: Where training data, enterprise records and agent memory live.
layers.bottleneck_now: Provenance and permission. EU marking duties and training-data disclosure laws are turning data lineage into a compliance cost.
layers.business_model: Usage-based storage and query fees, plus paid data labelling and licensing.
layers.structural_bottleneck: Permissioned, high-quality and expert-labelled data, and the cost of moving it.
layers.question_to_watch: If agents create most new databases, who becomes the default data layer for them?

layers.name: Foundation models
layers.subtitle: The labs that train the general-purpose models.
layers.bottleneck_now: Training cost against price. Per-token prices fell again while valuations rose, so the lead has to be refunded by capital.
layers.business_model: Per-token API fees and seat subscriptions, with open weights used as a distribution and ecosystem play.
layers.structural_bottleneck: Training compute, post-training talent and holding a lead while list prices fall.
layers.question_to_watch: Does the open-weight gap keep narrowing, and does it matter once price per task is near zero?

layers.name: Enablers and tools
layers.subtitle: Software that turns a model into something a team can ship.
layers.bottleneck_now: Independence. Cursor went to SpaceX, Hugging Face is going to Nvidia and Turso went to Supabase, so tooling is being absorbed upward.
layers.business_model: Developer subscriptions, usage fees and platform bundles that sit between the model and the product.
layers.structural_bottleneck: Evaluation, reliability and permissions for agents that act, plus being squeezed by the model vendors.
layers.question_to_watch: Do coding-agent tools stay independent, or are they absorbed by the labs and the chip vendors?

sources.label: SpaceX completes Cursor deal, Bloomberg Law

layers.name: Applications
layers.subtitle: Products that sell finished work to a business or a consumer.
layers.bottleneck_now: Proof of return. Large rounds went to EliseAI, Armadin and Instinct, and the open question is retention and deployment capacity.
layers.business_model: Seat plus usage pricing, drifting toward outcome-based pricing for agentic work.
layers.structural_bottleneck: Proving return on investment, distribution into the enterprise, and margin squeezed by model costs.
layers.question_to_watch: Which pricing model wins for agents, the seat, the task or the outcome?

layers.name: Capital
layers.subtitle: Who pays for the build, and on what terms.
layers.bottleneck_now: Concentration. A few names can raise at will while the rest of the stack leans on debt and strategic money.
layers.business_model: Equity at rising marks, strategic money from suppliers, and a growing share of asset-backed debt.
layers.structural_bottleneck: Concentration in a handful of labs, and the cost of debt for data centre builders.
layers.question_to_watch: Does a $1.4 trillion mark for OpenAI hold, and what does it do to everyone priced against it?

layers.name: Rules and policy
layers.subtitle: Law, export control and standards that gate deployment.
layers.bottleneck_now: Jurisdiction. The EU is fixing dates for transparency, and in the US federal action and state law are in open conflict.
layers.business_model: Compliance cost for deployers, licensing for exporters, and disclosure duties for model developers.
layers.structural_bottleneck: Fragmentation across jurisdictions and unresolved federal versus state authority in the US.
layers.question_to_watch: Do the courts let federal action override state AI laws before the EU deadlines bite?

markets_sowhat.compute: On-demand H100 rates still differ by {ratio} times for the same chip, from {lo_price} at {lo_provider} to {hi_price} at {hi_provider}. Nebius moved up on 1 October while AWS has held $6.88 per GPU-hour since its June 2025 cut, so today's cheapest provider may not stay cheapest.
markets_sowhat.capital: Money is abundant at the very top, where the largest items are acquisitions and lab rounds. Below that, rounds of $150M to $1B went to applications, world models, agent databases and GPU clouds, and GMI Cloud leaned on debt for two thirds of its raise.
markets_sowhat.models: Prices fell at every new Anthropic tier and Google is discounting Gemini 3.8 Flash through 31 December. Open-weight releases from Xiaomi and DeepSeek narrow the gap to the closed frontier, though the DeepSeek license is not yet confirmed.
markets_sowhat.energy: Power is now booked on twenty-year terms and turbines years in advance, so the next gigawatt goes to whoever signed early.

Protect open-source AI developers who rely on the platform. Includes up to $1B retention equity.
Reach more people and keep developing a personal agent that handles everyday tasks.

policies.title: AI Act Digital Omnibus changes the high-risk timetable
policies.body: Stand-alone high-risk systems such as hiring and credit scoring move from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027. AI built into regulated products moves to 2 Aug 2028. Article 50 transparency duties still apply from 2 Aug 2026, with marking for earlier systems due by 2 Dec 2026.

policies.title: Executive order targets state AI laws
policies.body: Sets up a DOJ litigation task force to challenge state AI laws, asks Commerce to classify them, and ties some federal funding to state AI rules. It carves out child safety, compute infrastructure and state procurement. Exact signing date was not confirmed in the source.

policies.title: Voluntary pre-release access to frontier models
policies.body: Creates a voluntary framework for developers to give government early access to frontier models up to 30 days before release. It also directs Homeland Security to issue cyber directives and build a classified benchmark for cyber capability. Reported by a law firm and not checked against the order text.

policies.title: Colorado rewrites its AI Act and a court pauses enforcement
policies.body: SB 26-189 replaces the 2024 law, drops impact assessments and applies to decisions made on or after 1 Jan 2027, with attorney general enforcement only. A federal court order in X.AI v. Weiser bars enforcement while an injunction request is pending, and its wording may reach the new law.

policies.title: SB 53 frontier transparency law is live
policies.body: Requires developers training models above 10^26 FLOPs to publish transparency information. AB 2013 on training-data disclosure took effect the same day.

policies.title: H200 and MI325X to China move to case-by-case licensing
policies.body: BIS replaced a presumption of denial for chips under set performance and bandwidth thresholds. Conditions include a 25 percent surcharge, independent US lab testing and a cap at half of US volumes. Reported by a secondary source.

policies.title: Cybersecurity Law gains its first AI clause
policies.body: The amended law adds AI governance for the first time, covering support for compute and training data alongside ethics, risk assessment and security oversight. Fines run up to RMB 10 million for critical infrastructure operators.

notes.history: Points are published list prices on the dates shown. The line is held flat between observations, so a step marks the date a change was first observed and not necessarily the date it happened. Filled dots come from an official page or announcement. Hollow dots are secondary mirrors, press reports or derived values and say so on hover. Lambda's 2023 point is an 8-GPU instance rate and its 2026 points are from a page that does not state instance size. Hyperscaler rates are per-instance prices divided by eight.
notes.spread: Hatched bars with an outline are Secondary, taken from a third-party mirror of the provider list. Hyperscaler bars are instance price divided by eight. No H200 rate was verified for AWS, Azure or Lambda, and no B200 rate for Azure.
notes.gpu_table: Hyperscalers price one 8-GPU instance per hour, so the per-GPU column divides the instance rate by eight. Lambda and Nebius price each GPU. Prices exclude tax, networking and storage. The AWS B200 row is indicative only.
notes.storage_table: Nebius bills per GiB and Google per GiB-hour, converted here at 730 hours a month. Cloudflare bills per GB. AWS S3 Standard is not shown because its rate could not be verified from the official page on the check date.
notes.models: Prices are per million tokens as published by each developer. Benchmark figures are vendor reported unless stated. Release dates marked Secondary come from a release tracker and not from the developer.
notes.capital: Deal size on a log scale. Bars start at $100M, so lengths compare ratios and not absolute amounts. The OpenAI row is a press report of early talks and not a closed round.
notes.policy: Effective and deadline dates on a single axis. The shaded band is the next 90 days from the issue date.

about.name: Esther Suebsubanant

about.thread: Corporate venture and M&A work taught her to follow the scarce input in every deal, and her EIPER work on compute and energy applies the same habit to the AI stack.
about.short: AI Radar is written by Esther Suebsubanant, an MBA and MS candidate at Stanford who built a corporate venture fund at Thai Union and advised on more than 30 cross-border M&A deals.

methodology: AI Radar is a human-curated weekly brief. Figures are transcribed from official pages on the check date, and each carries its source link. Where an official page draws prices only in the browser, the figure comes from a third-party mirror and is marked Secondary. Chart points that are derived are marked as derived. Anything that could not be confirmed is left out and not estimated. Prices change without notice, so verify in the provider console before purchasing.

energy.title: Google books about 3.6 GW of nuclear power from Constellation
energy.body: The agreement covers power from 11 nuclear plants. 890 MW starts in 2028 on a 20-year term, and Constellation plans more than $4.3B of upgrades to the plants. Google says it will carry its own power costs instead of passing them to other customers.

energy.title: Gas turbine queue reaches 116 GW as orders more than double
energy.body: GE Vernova's backlog and slot reservations rose from 100 GW to 116 GW in one quarter, with customer talks running to 2032 and beyond. Data center orders passed $5B so far this year, more than double all of 2025.

energy.title: The largest US grid market clears at its price cap again
energy.body: The 2028 to 2029 capacity auction cleared at the $325 per MW-day maximum. Data center demand was the main driver, and PJM forecasts peak demand rising by 66,000 MW by 2036. Pennsylvania households face an estimated $220 to $320 a year in extra costs.

energy.title: FERC orders every grid operator to justify its data center hookup rules
energy.body: Six show cause orders require each regional grid operator to defend or revise how large loads connect and how data centers share sites with power plants. The outcome decides how fast a new campus can get on the grid.
